title.en: Practical 1: Weight of an object by the principle of moments

text.en: A balanced metre scale can reveal an unknown weight.

The aim is to determine the weight of an object using the principle of moments. The apparatus is a metre scale, a knife edge, slotted weights and thread.
Support the metre scale at its centre of gravity so that it is horizontal. Hang a known weight W2 and an unknown weight W1 on either side. Fix one hanger and adjust the other until the scale balances, then measure the distances d1 and d2 from the centre and repeat for different positions.
At balance, anticlockwise moment equals clockwise moment: W1 x d1 = W2 x d2, so the unknown weight W1 = (W2 x d2) / d1. Take the mean of readings and write the result in kg wt.
